body: The frequency of inherited variants can change across generations. One mechanism is natural selection. In a particular environment, individuals with different inherited traits can differ in how many descendants they leave. A variant contributing to greater reproductive success can become more frequent.

Frequency can also change by chance, especially in small populations. That process is genetic drift. Mutation creates new variants, and gene flow moves variants between populations. Shared features and genetic comparisons provide evidence for common ancestry.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: An advantageous trait in one environment can be costly in another. Evolution has no fixed destination. Several mechanisms can operate on the same population at once.
purpose: Explain how heritable variation and population change contribute to diversity.
